title: Photographs for description: spice market, rain on a window
subject: English Language
source: Written for english-language/y10 lesson 18 (Photographs for description: spice market, rain on a window (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 18: Description: sensory detail, imagery and one clear viewpoint. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

head: Not this
This
rows: I could see stalls. I could hear people. I could smell spices. I could feel the heat. I could taste dust.
The spice sacks slumped open like tired mouths, breathing cumin into air already thick with heat.

blocks.h: Upgrading a detail into an image

head: Plain
Precise
Image
rows: The door was cracked and grey.
The door had gone grey with waiting, its paint peeling like old skin.
Rain needled the window, then slid away in silver threads.
Carts jostled like impatient cattle at a gate.

panels.title: One viewpoint
points: Only describe what you could notice from there
Move the lens, not the body

keywords.def: language that creates a picture in the reader's mind
choosing only the details that matter
weather or setting reflecting a mood

questions.q: Upgrade into an image: 'The street was quiet.'
questions.a: For example: The street held its breath; only a loose sign ticked against its post.

questions.q: Write one sentence of pathetic fallacy for a tense mood.
questions.a: For example: Clouds pressed down on the rooftops like a lid on a pot about to boil.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write a paragraph describing a spice market at midday from one viewpoint, using two senses and two images. Starter: 'From the shade of the archway...'
questions.a: One viewpoint, two senses, two images, a consistent mood.

questions.q: Extend: underline each image and name the method (simile, metaphor, personification).
Stretch: add a sound that contrasts with the main mood.
questions.a: For example: a sudden clatter of a dropped tray that breaks the heavy stillness.

questions.q: Which sentence has the best selected sensory detail?
options: I could see rain and hear rain and feel cold.
It was a very rainy and wet and cold night.
Rain needled the window, then slid away in silver threads.
questions.a: C) Rain needled the window, then slid away in silver threads.. It chooses two senses and turns them into an image; the others list or repeat.
B) weather or setting to reflect mood
options: weather or setting to reflect mood

questions.q: Answer the ponder in one sentence.
questions.a: Often smell or touch; without them description feels flat and only visual.
